title: Emptying, rinsing and storing a mop bucket
audience: Cleaners who finish wet mopping and need to empty, rinse and store a bucket and wringer correctly.
learningOutcomes: Drain and flush a bucket and wringer at a sluice without spilling dirty water on the floor.
Lift a heavy bucket safely using the handle and the rim, with the knees bent.
Store the bucket and wringer clean and dry in the cleaning cupboard.

instruction.heading: Why the bucket needs a proper finish
instruction.body: A bucket that is left with dirty water, grit or product residue in it becomes the source of the soil you thought you had removed. The next time it is filled, the residue dissolves into fresh solution and goes back onto the floor. The finish of the job is therefore part of the cleaning, not an extra. Empty the water, rinse the bucket and wringer, and dry them before storage.

instruction.heading: Empty at a sluice, not a corridor
instruction.body: Take the bucket to a sluice or a utility sink, which is designed to take dirty water. Remove the wringer first and rinse it under cold water, wiping off soil and product residue. Leave the wringer to one side, clear of the working zone, so that it cannot collect dirt in transit. Pour the water out at the sink, never onto the floor.

instruction.heading: Lifting safely
instruction.body: Use your legs, not your back. Keep one hand on the handle and the other on the rear lip of the base, bring the load close to your body, and tip it into the sink from the back edge. If the bucket has a drain tap in its lower back, open the tap into the sink instead of lifting the bucket at all. For a heavy bucket, ask for help rather than straining.

instruction.heading: Rinse, dry and store
instruction.body: Run a hose from the sink tap into the bucket, working from the rear to the front so the water carries grime away from you. Rinse the sides as well. Dry the bucket inside and out with a cloth, drop the wringer back in, and store the bucket in the designated area of the cleaning cupboard. Leave the bucket upright and clear of the floor to dry.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection before handling the bucket and wringer.
Carry the bucket to a sluice or utility basin.
Remove the wringer, rinse it with cold water at the sink, and wipe it.
Place the wringer clear of the working zone.
With the knees bent, lift the bucket by its handle and rear rim and empty the dirty water into the sink. If the bucket has a drain tap, open the tap instead.
Hose the bucket out, rear first, then the sides.
Dry the bucket inside and out with a cloth.
Place the wringer back in the bucket and store the assembly in the designated closet area, upright and off the floor.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner tips a full bucket of grey water onto the corridor floor outside the closet to save time, then rinses the bucket on the floor.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is wrong with this, and what should have been done?
workedExamples.reasoning: Tipping dirty water onto a corridor floor spreads soil and creates a slip hazard, and rinsing on the floor puts residue back into the work area. The bucket should have been carried to the sluice, emptied over the sink, and rinsed there. The floor should be cleaned up immediately if water has been spilled.

workedExamples.situation: A bucket with a drain tap is in the cleaning cupboard. The cleaner has been lifting it over the sink every time, and it is awkward and heavy to carry.
workedExamples.reasoning: Use the drain tap to empty the bucket into the sink, so that the bucket does not have to be lifted full. Still lift the bucket by its handle and rim with the knees bent for the rinse and the return to the closet.

equipmentAndPpe: Hose connected to a tap, with a suitable nozzle.
Cloth for drying the bucket and wringer.
Designated storage area in the cleaning cupboard.

commonErrors.error: Emptying dirty water onto a corridor or into a non-drain area.
commonErrors.prevention: Carry the bucket to a sluice or utility basin and empty it there.

commonErrors.error: Lifting a full bucket with a bent back, or twisting while carrying it.
commonErrors.prevention: Flex the knees, keep the load close, and use a drain tap where the bucket has one.

commonErrors.error: Storing a damp bucket with the wringer inside, which encourages odour and residue.
commonErrors.prevention: Dry the bucket on all sides before storing it upright and clear of the floor.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Lift with the legs and keep the load close to the body. Ask for help with a heavy or full bucket.
Wear gloves when handling dirty water and wringers, and wash hands after the task.
Clean up any spilled water immediately, and set out a wet floor sign if a spill cannot be cleared at once.

qualityStandard: The bucket and wringer are empty, rinsed and dry before storage.
No dirty water or residue is left in the bucket or spread across the floor.
The bucket is stored in its designated location, upright and off the floor.
No spill is left on the floor at the far end of the task.
documentationEvidence: Equipment check record where the site keeps one, noting a bucket or wringer that is cracked, leaking or needs replacing.
summary: Empty and rinse the bucket at a sluice, never on the floor.
Flex the knees and use the drain tap where one is fitted.
Dry the bucket on all sides before storing it upright.
Report any cracked, leaking or worn equipment rather than using it.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should dirty mop water be emptied?
options: The corridor floor, where it can dry quickly
A sluice or utility basin designed for dirty water
A potted plant near the closet door

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is the bucket rinsed and dried before it is stored?
options: So that the bucket can be stored with the wringer inside it wet for the next shift
So that the bucket will not need to be lifted next time and the floor stays dry
So that residue and soil are not carried into the next fill and back onto the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: How should a heavy, full bucket be lifted to empty it?
options: Flex the knees, hold the handle and rim, and ask for help if it is too heavy
Bend at the waist and lift it quickly with one hand and carry it to the sink
Twist the body while carrying it to the sink with the load held high
